title: Mujaddara
skill: Lentils and rice cooked together, crispy onions

notes.text: Fry the onions in two batches, so they crisp instead of steaming.

move.title: A legume and a grain in one pot
move.body: Mujaddara is brown lentils and rice cooked together with cumin, under a big pile of onions fried slowly until they're dark and crisp. Lentils take longer than rice, so they get a head start. Today you'll time the two to finish together, fry the onions low and slow, and cook the rice in some of the onion oil.

callback.body: In red lentil soup, you cooked lentils until they fell apart. Brown lentils keep their shape longer, and here you stop them halfway, while they're still firm, so they finish in the pot with the rice.

why.title: Give the lentils a head start
why.body: Brown lentils take about 25 minutes to cook; rice takes about 15. Simmered alone first for 12 minutes, the lentils catch up, and the two finish together.

why.title: Low and slow for crisp onions
why.body: Onions are mostly water. On medium heat, the water steams out first while they soften, then their sugars brown, and then they crisp. Rushed on high heat, the edges burn while the middles are still wet.

why.title: Salt the onions after
why.body: Salt pulls water out of onions. Salted while they fry, they steam and go soft. Salted on the paper towels, they stay crisp.

why.title: Cook the rice in onion oil
why.body: The oil the onions fried in tastes of them. Toasting the rice in a few spoonfuls of it carries that flavor all through the pot.

why.title: Lid on, hands off
why.body: The rice and lentils finish in the steam trapped under the lid. Lifting it lets the steam out; stirring breaks the rice. Set the timer and leave it.

wrong.sign: Some onions burned while others are still pale
wrong.fix: The heat was too high, or they weren't stirred enough. Turn the heat down, stir more often, and take out the dark ones as they're done.

wrong.sign: The onions are soft, not crisp
wrong.fix: The pan was crowded, or they came out too early. Fry them a few minutes longer in smaller batches, until they're dark brown.
They simmered too long before the rice went in. It still tastes good; next time drain them at 12 minutes, while they're firm.

wrong.sign: The rice is crunchy when the timer rings
wrong.fix: Sprinkle ¼ cup of hot water over the top, put the lid back on, and cook 5 more minutes on low.

quiz.q: Why do the lentils cook on their own first?
choices: They take longer than rice, so they need a head start
To make them soft enough to mash

quiz.q: Why are the onions fried on medium, not high?
choices: Their water has to cook out before they can crisp
quiz.explain: Rushed, the edges burn while the middles stay wet.

choices: After frying, on the paper towels
Before they go in the pan
quiz.explain: Salt pulls out water and makes them soft.

steps.text: Spread the lentils on the plate and pick out any tiny stones or shriveled lentils. Rinse them in the colander under cold water.

Put the lentils and the lentils' {qty:water} of water in the saucepan. Bring them to a boil, then turn the heat down and simmer with the lid off until they're just starting to soften but still hold their shape.
steps.look: A lentil pressed between your fingers, once it's cool, squashes but still has a little firm middle.
steps.tip: Slice the onions while the lentils simmer.

steps.text: Pour the lentils into the colander in the sink and let them drain.
Cut the onions in half through the root, peel them, and slice each half into thin half-moons, about ⅛ inch thick.
steps.look: Thin slices, all close to the same thickness.
steps.tip: Use the claw, knuckles against the blade.

steps.text: Put the rice in the medium bowl and cover it with cold water. Swish it with your hand, then carefully pour off the cloudy water, holding the rice back with your hand. Do this 3 times, and pour off as much water as you can.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the onions and cook, stirring every couple of minutes, until they're deep brown and crisp at the edges.
steps.look: Dark golden brown all over, and crisp when one cools.
steps.tip: They go slowly at first, then fast. Stir more often once they start to brown, and turn the heat down if the edges darken too quickly.

steps.text: Turn off the burner. Lift the onions out with the slotted spoon onto paper towels, spread them out, and sprinkle on the onions' salt. Carefully pour the oil left in the skillet into the heatproof bowl.
steps.tip: Hold the skillet with both hands and pour slowly, away from you.

steps.text: Spoon 3 tablespoons of the onion oil into the large pot and heat it over medium heat. Add the rice, cumin, cinnamon, and pepper and stir for 2 minutes, until the rice smells toasty.

Add the lentils, the rice's 2 cups of water, and its salt. Stir in a third of the onions. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to your lowest setting, put the lid on, and cook without lifting the lid.
Turn off the burner and leave the lid on. Let it rest.
Fluff it gently with the fork and taste; add a pinch more salt if it needs it. Pile it on a plate, heap the rest of the onions on top, and serve with yogurt if you like.
steps.look: The rice and lentils are tender and separate, with no water left in the pot.
steps.tip: Let the leftover onion oil cool and keep it in a jar in the fridge for up to a week. It's great for frying eggs.
